rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate pushes obfuscation coverage up across all seven passes while keeping cost weights moderate. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain since the workload is dominated by small display-style member functions (241-441 bytes) whose control flow flattens cleanly and whose loop bodies are short enough that dispatcher overhead stays acceptable; BCF and ICALL follow, with ICALL targeting the virtual-heavy C++ call sites in the supervisor/consultant/programmer hierarchy to obscure call-graph edges, and BCF adding opaque predicates that remain cheap given only 15 functions and ~2KB of text, so both size and runtime budgets are generous. SPLIT is kept enabled with low cost weights because subdividing the larger display methods increases the number of basic blocks FLA and BCF can scramble, acting as a force multiplier rather than a standalone defense. SUB and IGV carry modest SecurityGain but high DiversityGain: instruction substitution is nearly free and diversifies arithmetic in the small helpers, and IGV hides the vtable/global references typical of this polymorphic benchmark. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept uniformly low (0.1-0.3) to reflect that round 0 showed the toolchain handles this sample robustly, while RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights around 0.4-0.6 for the expensive passes keep them from over-triggering on tiny cold helpers where overhead would be pure waste.
